interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s energy system is currently operating in an exceptional low-carbon state, anchored by 4.4 GW of active wind generation. This substantial renewable volume has driven regional carbon intensity down to a clean 32 gCO2/kWh, demonstrating the immense capability of Scotland’s generation fleet to displace thermal generation. However, this operational high point simultaneously exposes persistent infrastructure bottlenecks across the wider transmission network. With total wasted energy reaching 221.1 MWh, export limitations—principally across the congested B6 boundary into England—are actively forcing renewable curtailment to preserve system balance and stability. 

While the near-zero carbon intensity reflects outstanding environmental performance, the volume of discarded energy represents a distinct commercial inefficiency. Mitigating this 221.1 MWh loss requires targeted grid modernization, including accelerated transmission reinforcements, utility-scale battery energy storage systems, and enhanced dynamic demand response. Without these structural flexibility upgrades, periods of high wind output will consistently generate localized surpluses that cannot reach key demand centers. Prioritizing capital deployment into boundary capacity and co-located storage is essential to monetize this stranded clean power, lower overall balancing mechanism costs, and unlock the full economic potential of Scotland’s renewable assets.
